      🩺 Self-Check

      A quick, non-destructive test of the planner's core logic — date math, saving/loading, carry-forward, reminders, and more — and a read-through of everything stored, to find anything damaged before you open it. It never changes your data unless you choose Repair or Restore for a problem it lists.

      📦 Storage Health

      Your planner data lives in this browser, which has a size limit. This shows how much you're using and lets you archive old weeks to stay well clear of it.

      Archive old weeks

      Bundle weeks older than a date into a downloaded file and remove them from this device to free space. Nothing is lost — restore any of them later with "⬆ Restore from file". The current week is never archived.

      🕑 Automatic Snapshots

      The planner quietly keeps the last several days as snapshots so you can roll back if something goes wrong — no need to remember to export. Snapshots live on this device alongside your data. For protection against the whole browser being cleared, still download a Backup file now and then.

      ⚙️ Setup

      Turn features on or off to fit how you work. Start small and add more anytime — hiding a section never deletes anything; your data stays and reappears when you switch it back on.

      🔠 Text size on this device — Comfortable is easier for long sessions; Compact fits more on screen:
      💾 Where this planner saves & syncs:
      ⬇ Backup location: Downloads folder (default)
      🗓 Weekly backup into that folder (a dated file, the newest 8 kept):
      ☑ Checklist templates: reusable lists you can attach to any task (packing lists, routines, procedures)
      📲 Phone app — the planner on your phone, synced through OneDrive
      📲 Install on this device — run the planner as an app with its own icon
      🔔 Daily notification: one summary of what's due, even when the planner is in a background tab
      🏷 Time tracking categories: set up or rename the job types and subtypes the Track dropdowns offer
      📥 Project Tracker: pull tasks you sent from the Project Tracker app
      📥 Unscheduled — from Project Tracker

      Tasks sent from Project Tracker that had no due date. Give one a date to drop it onto that day's Daily 3 list, or remove it. Placing a task moves it off this list.

      🏷 Categories & subcategories

      One category per line; indent its subcategories beneath it. This is the list the Track dropdowns offer — add names here rather than waiting to log a session first.

      To rename something and update sessions you have already logged, write Old name -> New name. A plain edit only changes the list, leaving past entries under the old name.

      ☑ Checklist templates

      Reusable lists you can attach to any task — packing lists, routines, procedures. Attaching one makes an independent copy, so ticking it off never changes the template.

      Bulk edit — every template at once

      Start a template with == Name ==, optionally @ Category, then # for a section, one step per line, - for a sub-step and > for a note. Saving replaces the whole library, so anything removed here is removed. Checklists already attached to tasks are independent copies and are never affected.

      Sections collapse — click a heading to fold it away.

      One step per line. # starts a section · - makes a sub-step of the line above · > adds a note (guidance, not a tick-box).

      📋 Weekly Review
      —

      A quick five-question ritual to close out the week. Each answer flows into the right spot in your planner automatically.

      Goes into Week in Review → Progress This Week.

      Added to Roadblocks → What Slipped. The "why" matters more than the "what" — patterns hide here.

      Added to Week in Review → Acknowledge yourself. The most-skipped item — this is where you build resilience.

      Added to Roadblocks → Time-Sinks. Recurring time-sinks across weeks reveal what to delegate, automate, or eliminate.

      Sent to the Top 3 list for the date you choose below, with a [Next week's #1] prefix.

      Anything from this week's Calls & Emails and Meetings & Appointments that wasn't checked off. Carry the ones still worth doing into next week individually.

      Every open Mind Dump item whose reminder has been pushed at least three times. Decide each one now: do it, hand it off, drop it, or keep it. Whatever is still stuck is entered under Doing What's Hard when next week is created. Changes here apply straight away.

      Welcome to your Weekly Planner 👋
      Three things get you productive today. Everything else can wait.
      1. 1
        📌 Write your Daily Top 3
        Click 📌 Top 3 at the top and type the three things that matter most today. Tick them off as you go — anything unfinished moves to tomorrow’s notes on its own, so nothing gets lost.
      2. 2
        🧠 Empty your head into the Mind Dump
        Everything else lives here — tasks, ideas, things to buy — split into Business and Personal. Give each item a number from 1 (do it tomorrow) to 5 (someday), and 7 when it’s done.
      3. 3
        ✓ Save when you’re done
        Your typing is saved automatically as you go, and the planner keeps daily snapshots you can roll back to. Press Ctrl/Cmd + S any time you want to be certain.
      ⚙️ Only see what you need. Quarterly planning, Reminders, Promises and more are switched off to keep things simple — turn on what you want in ⚙️ Setup (top-right), where you can also make the text bigger.
      💡 Shortcuts: Ctrl/Cmd + K searches everything · Ctrl/Cmd + J adds a task from anywhere.
      🔎 Search Everything
      Type at least 2 characters to search.
      🖨 Print
      Choose what to print. Expand a tab to pick its sections. Your selections are remembered.
      Save This Week
      Choose where to keep your weekly data. Your choice is remembered for next time.
      💾 Browser only
      Stays in this browser on this device. Fastest, but won't transfer if you switch computers.
      📁 Browser + hard drive
      A JSON file is also saved to a folder on your computer — keep backups, sync via Dropbox/iCloud, or open in another tool.
      Save location
      No folder chosen
      Your browser doesn't support direct folder access — the file will download to your Downloads folder each time you save.

      ☁️ Set up Cloud Sync

      Pick one JSON file inside a folder synced by OneDrive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive, or any cloud-sync service. The planner will read from it on open and write to it on every save.

      Use this when you want your data to follow you between browsers (Edge ↔ Brave) or between computers (home ↔ work). Same file = same data, everywhere it syncs.

      ⚠ One machine at a time.
      Sync services don't merge — they replace. If you edit on two machines simultaneously, whichever saves last wins, and the other's file becomes a "CONFLICT" copy. Close the planner on one machine before opening it on another for cleanest results.
      1. Open your OneDrive (or Dropbox) folder.
      2. Decide on a filename like sentrybox-planner.json.
      3. Click the button below. The browser will ask you to pick a file:
        • First-time setup: navigate to your OneDrive folder, type the filename in the "File name" box, and click Save.
        • Already exists on another machine: navigate to your OneDrive folder and pick the existing file.

      Get it out of your head, onto the page.
      Saved
      💾 Setup
      Dates Overdue Today Upcoming Someday Status 6 Cancelled 7 Done 8 Failed 9 Delegated
      Get it out of your head. List everything in no particular order, then give each item a reminder date. Items carry forward from week to week automatically.
      Dates. Click a date to push it on by the same interval, counted from today. ▾ changes it or adds a hard due date, which a push can never pass.
      ↻ Pushed. Shows how many times an item has been put off. At three it asks you to decide: do it, hand it off, or drop it.
      Boxes. The round green box means done. The small square selects a row for Move, Archive or Delete. ★ marks it important.
      Status. 6, 7 and 8 archive the item; use Show Archived to see it again. 9 records who it was handed to.
      Keyboard. With the cursor in a row: Alt+R sets a reminder, Alt+S toggles the star. Ctrl+J is Quick Add.
